records.text: In the year that King Oziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up; and the house was full of His glory.
And seraphim stood around Him: each one had six wings, and each one had six wings; with two they covered their faces, and with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
And one cried to another, saying: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; all the earth is full of His glory.
And the lintel was lifted at the sound of their cry, and the house was filled with smoke.
And I said, Woe is me, for I am pierced to the heart! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Sabaoth.
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.
If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.
And say to this people: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have set before your face the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine; whoever goes out to join the Chaldeans who have shut you in will live, and his life will be spoil, and he will live.
Because I have fixed My face upon this city for evils and not for good things. It will be handed into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will burn it down with fire.
Will the earth not be disturbed over these things, and everyone dwelling in it mourn? A consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.
“On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at midday, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime.

I will turn your festivals to mourning and all your songs to lamentation. I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head; I will make him like mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain.
Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will send famine upon the earth: not famine for bread or thirst for water, but famine for hearing the Lord’s word.
Waters will be shaken as far as the sea, and from north to east they will run about seeking the Lord’s word, but certainly will not find it.
On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst,
those who swear by Samaria’s propitiation and say, ‘Your god lives, Dan!’ and ‘Your god lives, Beersheba!’ They will fall and certainly never rise again.”

making all things and refashioning them, turning death’s shadow into morning and darkening day into night; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name,
the One distributing shattering against strength and bringing suffering upon a fortress.
It is reckoned a land of Rephaim; for the Rephaim dwelt there aforetime, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a nation great and numerous and mightier than you, like the Anakim. And the Lord destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who inherited the land and dwelt in their stead unto this day,
even as they did for the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, when they blotted out the Horites from before them, and inherited the land, and dwelt in their stead unto this day.
And the Hivites who dwelt in settlements as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came forth from Cappadocia blotted them out, and dwelt in their stead.
“I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Behold, I am bringing a nation upon you from far away, house of Israel, says the Lord, a nation whose language’s sound you will not understand.
All are strong,

and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.
And it will be in those days, says the Lord your God: I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.
You turned away from Me, says the Lord; you will go backward. And I will stretch out My hand and destroy you, and I will no longer let them go.
And I will scatter them in a dispersion; at My people’s gates they were bereaved; they destroyed My people because of their evils.
Their widows multiplied beyond the sea’s sand. I brought misery upon a young man’s mother at noon; suddenly I cast trembling and haste upon her.

Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.
After they fell silent, James spoke: “Men, brothers, listen to me.
Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name.
With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:
‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright,
so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
known from long ago.’
On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.
Egypt will become desolate, and Idumea a desolate plain, because of injustices concerning the sons of Judah, because they poured out righteous blood in their land.
But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generations upon generations.
“I will avenge their blood, and I will certainly not acquit.” And the Lord will dwell in Zion.
Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.
The devastated land will be worked, instead of lying devastated before every passerby’s eyes.
They will say, “That devastated land has become like a garden of delight, and the deserted, devastated, razed cities stand fortified.”
The nations remaining around you will know that I, the Lord, have rebuilt the razed places and planted the devastated places. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.
I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them in My anger, wrath, and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in confidence.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me always, for their good and their children’s good after them.
I will establish an eternal covenant with them, which I will certainly not turn back from behind them. I will put My fear in their heart so that they do not depart from Me.
I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.
